diagnosis: The issue lies in the `is_token_end` function where the handling of comments and subsequent tokens is flawed. Specifically, when encountering a semicolon (`;`) followed by other characters, the code incorrectly treats all following content as part of the comment until the end of the line, preventing proper tokenization of subsequent valid tokens.

causal_chain: The failing test cases show that after a semicolon, subsequent tokens are either misclassified or ignored.
In `is_token_end`, when `str_com_id` is less than 2 (indicating a comment), the function returns true upon encountering a newline (`\n`).
However, this logic doesn't account for cases where characters after the semicolon should be treated as separate tokens.
mr_refs: MR2: Deleting content after `;` shouldn't affect token counts but it does.
MR4: Random case changes and comment removals still cause errors in tokenization.
testcase_refs:
source_s4_mr2: Input ';6#l
93' outputs an error for '6#l' instead of recognizing '93'

followup_s2_mr5: Input 'xor 
;;bWJ00dn...' misclassifies 'xor ' as an error

repair_candidates.assumption: Modify `is_token_end` to correctly handle cases where a semicolon is followed by other tokens.

edits.rationale: Adjust the condition to ensure that only content until the next newline after `;` is treated as a comment.
edits.replacement: if(str_com_id<2) { if(ch=='\n') return(TRUE); else if(ch==';') { ch=get_char(tp); while(ch!='\n' && ch!=EOF) { ch=get_char(tp); } return(TRUE); } else return(FALSE); }

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Fixes the tokenization after semicolons by properly limiting comment scope to until newline or next `;`.
preservation_constraints: Passing test cases where comments are correctly handled.
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Correctly limit comment processing to only content between `;` and the next newline.

repair_candidates.assumption: Enhance the buffer handling in `get_token` to prevent premature termination of token reading after semicolons.

edits.rationale: Ensure that after ungetting a character, subsequent reads correctly capture tokens following comments.

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Improves buffer management to correctly read tokens following comments.
preservation_constraints: Passing test cases where token reading after comments works as expected.
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Improve character ungetting and subsequent token reading logic.

edits.rationale: Ensure that semicolon is treated as a standalone special symbol without affecting subsequent tokenization.

preservation_constraints: Passing test cases where special symbols are correctly identified.
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Clarify the treatment of semicolons as special symbols without affecting token continuity.

edits.rationale: Add checks to ensure that errors in token parsing do not disrupt subsequent token processing.

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Makes error handling more robust so that one misparsed token doesn't cause all subsequent tokens to fail.
preservation_constraints: Passing test cases where errors in parsing do not affect other tokens.
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Improve error reporting without disrupting overall token stream processing.

repair_candidates.assumption: Refactor the `get_token` function to use a state machine approach for better control flow.

edits.rationale: Replace current logic with a state machine that explicitly tracks token boundaries, especially after semicolons and comments.
edits.replacement: enum states { INIT, STRING, COMMENT }; int state = INIT; ... while (state != END) { switch(state) { case INIT: if(ch=='"') state=STRING; else if(ch==59) state=COMMENT; break; case STRING: if(ch=='"') state=INIT; break; case COMMENT: if(ch=='\n') state=INIT; break; } ... }

repair_candidates.expected_effect: Implements a more robust state management system for token parsing, especially around comments and special symbols.
preservation_constraints: Passing test cases where token transitions are correctly managed.
repair_candidates.repair_intent: Introduce a state machine to better manage token boundaries and transitions.

uncertainty: While the primary issue is in `is_token_end`, there may be multiple plausible fixes depending on how the state management and error handling are structured. The proposed candidates cover different angles of potential failure points, but further testing would be needed to confirm which provides complete reliability.
